item.title: What’s Driving Up Maine’s Energy Bills? Natural Gas
item.description: Natural gas, not solar panels and wind turbines, is the primary driver behind soaring power prices in Maine, according to a new report released this week by the state’s energy department.

item.title: Lamont Proposes Free Bus Rides For Veterans, Half Fares For Students
item.description: The $3.5 million investment recognizes the important service of the nation’s veterans, while also acknowledging the mobility needs of young students. The proposal is currently being considered by the legislature’s Appropriations Committee.

item.title: CT State Rep. Eyes Revisions To Early Parole Rules
item.description: Early parole in Connecticut is granted by the Board of Pardons and Paroles. Generally, a person sentenced to more than two years must serve half of their sentence for non-violent crimes or 85% of their sentence for violent crimes to be eligible. Those convicted of murder are not eligible for early parole.

item.title: Zullo Appointed Assistant Leader Of House Republican Caucus
item.description: State Rep. Joe Zullo, R-East Haven, has been elevated to serve as an assistant leader of the House Republican Caucus, party officials announced Wednesday.

item.title: Connecticut Pushes Earned Income Tax Credit Campaign as Thousands Miss Out On Benefits
item.description: The federal Earned Income Tax Credit is a refundable tax credit for low- to moderate-income workers. Families earning up to roughly $60,000 may qualify, depending on income and number of children.

item.title: CT Advocates Seek Limits On Some School Suspensions
item.description: “This is not about students not being held accountable for behavior,” state Rep. Anthony Nolan said. “This is about students being in school and getting the help they need to rebuild or relearn what techniques they need so they don't have any of these non-violent outbursts."

item.title: Nursing, Social Work Grad Students Could Get Student Loan Help Under Proposed CT Program
item.description: As of Feb. 5, the bill had been referred to the Joint Committee on Finance, Revenue and Bonding and a public hearing is expected in the coming weeks.

item.title: Opinion | In A Climate Of Cuts And Broken Trust, Nonprofits (119K To Zero Collective) Stand Firm For Our Young People
item.description: Leaders from five different nonprofits within the 119K To Zero Collective say recent news regarding the state audit of misappropriated funds in Hartford, combined with a harsh federal funding climate, have created a "perfect storm" for Connecticut’s nonprofit sector. Trust is being tested exactly when our services are most needed.

item.title: Blumenthal Bill Targets Gun Industry Advertising
item.description: The proposal, dubbed the Responsible Firearms Marketing Act would direct the Federal Trade Commission to launch an investigation into the advertising and marketing practices of gun manufacturers.

item.title: Agreement Reached In Free Speech Lawsuit
item.description: The ACLU Foundation of Connecticut and the Connecticut State Police have reached an agreement in a federal lawsuit over residents’ right to protest on highway overpasses.
